title: ～っぱなし — leaving ～ as it is
summary: Attached to a verb stem, it means leaving something in a state without taking care of it, or a state continuing for a long time. It often carries a negative feeling (careless or tiresome). Used in casual speech.

patterns.form: 動詞ます形（語幹）＋っぱなし
patterns.gloss: verb stem + っぱなし (つけっぱなし、開けっぱなし)

body.p: One is leaving something as is without doing what you should, such as not turning it off or not closing it (つけっぱなし, 開けっぱなし, 出しっぱなし). The other is a state that keeps going, as in 立ちっぱなし. Both imply a state that is not really good.

body.h: How to use it and cautions
body.p: It is used as 〜っぱなしにする, 〜っぱなしで or 〜っぱなしだ, and can link to the next clause, as in つけっぱなしで寝てしまった. It is close to 〜まま, but っぱなし carries a stronger sense of blame or hardship.

examples.ja: 電気（でんき）をつけっぱなしで寝（ね）てしまった。
examples.romaji: Denki o tsuke ppanashi de nete shimatta.
examples.tr: I fell asleep with the light left on.
examples.note: Left on without turning it off.

examples.ja: 窓（まど）を開（あ）けっぱなしにして出（で）かけてしまった。
examples.romaji: Mado o ake ppanashi ni shite dekakete shimatta.
examples.tr: I went out and left the window wide open.
examples.note: 〜っぱなしにする: to leave it that way.

examples.ja: 立（た）ちっぱなしで働（はたら）いたので、足（あし）がとても疲（つか）れた。
examples.romaji: Tachippanashi de hataraita node, ashi ga totemo tsukareta.
examples.tr: I worked standing the whole time, so my legs got really tired.

pitfalls: It is hard to use in a positive sense. Some uses such as 勝ちっぱなし exist, but basically it describes an unwelcome state.
Attach it to the verb stem: × つけるっぱなし, ○ つけっぱなし.
